purpose: Uneven natural rubble, collapsed chimneys, open dust patches

images.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Redesign this failed rubble sprite into believable FULLY COLLAPSED WWII city ruins, retaining its natural subdued painted game-art textures. The reference is edit target and only APPROXIMATE building-block footprint, NOT a layout to preserve brick-by-brick. CRITICAL: REMOVE ALL intact upright chimneys, square chimney mouths, ventilation stacks, neat rooftop equipment and intact roof panels. Chimneys have fallen and shattered: only 1-2 displaced irregular broken brick shaft fragments lying diagonally among debris, no repeating square holes at old chimney positions. Break the regular foundation grid; surviving wall stubs are discontinuous, jagged and low. Rubble is sparse and uneven, NOT a uniform carpet of bricks or roof tiles: 3-5 irregular concentrated heaps, one larger collapse mound, scattered small fragments with widely varied sizes and angles, several broad open dusty areas and dark irregular collapsed-cellar hollows. Around 35-45 percent of the interior remains open bare dusty/scorched ground or genuine transparent gaps allowing the underlying paving to show. Ground is matte dusty gray-brown, subtle soot; tile and brick fragments muted and small, NO neat rows, no repetitive patterns. A few broken heavy timber beams scattered at oblique angles, not a repeating lattice. Residential rubble: muted brick, small broken terracotta and slate shards, gray masonry, splintered timber; heavily broken and collapsed. STRICT 90-degree vertical orthographic OVERHEAD PLAN: no visible facade, no tilted perspective. Keep approximate group center and occupied area, same portrait canvas proportions and framing as the reference; keep the entire irregular rubble perimeter visible with margin, no hex clipping. Genuine transparent background outside debris group and in open gaps, no solid tile backing, no hex border, no text, no fire or smoke plumes. Strong large-scale uneven massing readable at 222x256 pixels. Destruction must change the silhouette and object arrangement visibly.
